name: Encoding Converter
description: Detect the encoding and line endings of text files and convert them in bulk, e.g. GBK to UTF-8
help: Add files or a folder (or drop them on the window). Each file's encoding is detected: byte order marks, UTF-16, UTF-8, and legacy encodings such as GBK, Big5 and Shift_JIS. Binary files are skipped.

Detection of legacy encodings is a guess. Click a file to preview it: if the text looks garbled, pick another encoding in its row until it reads correctly. A warning icon marks files that do not decode cleanly.
The preview also warns when a character cannot be stored in the target encoding (for example emoji in GBK); those files are reported as failed and left unchanged.
Converting in place writes each file safely through a temporary file and keeps a .bak copy unless you turn it off. Files that are already in the target form are not touched.
Line endings can be kept, or unified to LF (macOS / Linux) or CRLF (Windows). A BOM is only used with UTF-8 and UTF-16.
